report.summary: Both failures have one root cause in the app: `validate_book` in app/main.py:83 accepts a year up to `this_year + 1`, so a next-year book is saved (API returns 201, UI lists the 2027 row) when the tests expect a 422 and an error message. Fix the product bound to `this_year` (matching the message on line 84 and `test_current_year_is_accepted`), then rerun both tests.

causes.title: Server accepts books dated next year, contrary to its own validation message
causes.explanation: validate_book allows years up to this_year + 1, but its error message and the test contract say the maximum is the current year. Because the bound is computed from date.today(), the behaviour is deterministic: any run in any year accepts year = this_year + 1. The API test therefore gets 201 instead of 422, and the UI test never sees the error element because the book is saved and the page redirects to the list, which shows the 2027 row. The test expectations are consistent with each other and with test_current_year_is_accepted, so the test is right and the app is wrong.
evidence: app/main.py:84: `raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")` (message says max is this_year)
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:44: `expect(books.error).to_contain_text("Year must be between")` fails with `element(s) not found`
UI aria snapshot shows row `Future-d41404e1 Someone 2027 Delete`, so the book was persisted
tests/api/test_books_api.py:47-50 test_current_year_is_accepted expects THIS_YEAR to be accepted, which the code does
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py validate_book, change the upper bound to `this_year` (`if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year:`). Optionally make the message and bound share one expression. Then rerun tests/api/test_books_api.py and tests/ui/test_books_ui.py. Check that no other code or seed data relies on next-year books being accepted.
